title: Regional failover animator: health certification and rollback plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an orchestrated multi-region failover controller (the 'animator') that validates standby clusters before traffic promotion and provides deterministic rollback directives when health gates fail. This ticket covers: 1) health certification criteria for standby nodes (probe types, KV cache warm metrics, sequence latency percentiles, model variant compatibility checks); 2) choreography for promoting and demoting regions with minimal customer impact and no cold-start regressions; 3) automated rollback and bumpback plan when health gates are violated during canary or surge; 4) integration points with routing policy engine, capacity inventory, and Console SLO dashboards. Deliverables: design doc, probe implementation, CI job for probe regression, control-plane API to trigger certification and forced rollback, runbook updates, and at least two end-to-end chaos tests in staging that simulate region outage and partial capacity degradation.
acceptance_criteria: Standby certification API returns PASS/FAIL with a diagnostic payload within 6s for typical cluster sizes
Promotion flow only routes production traffic to a standby region after certification PASS and before thresholded ramp (ramp configured by policy)
Automated rollback triggers when any of the configured gates are breached (KV warm hit rate < 75%, p95 generation latency > 1.8x baseline, failed model variant fallback > 10% of requests)

Two chaos scenarios in staging: full-region-DR (simulate AZ/region fail) and partial GPU pool loss; both show successful failover with no more than 2x token-latency increase for <5% of requests and successful rollback during injected regressions
Console shows an annotated trace and cost delta for the failover window and the runbook has step-by-step rollback commands validated by oncall
tasks: Draft design doc: certification gates, metrics, and control-plane API (link to Confluence in links)
Implement health probes: KV cache priming probe, sequence-latency synthetic probe, model-variant compatibility smoke test
Extend routing engine to accept certification tokens and enforce tier-based promotion (tier routing policies)
Add fallback model-variant policy: prefer quantized low-cost variant if primary not available, with configurable quality guardrails
Wire telemetry: SLO events, certification audit log, and Console annotation hooks
Create CI/regression test that fails when probe flakiness exceeds threshold
Author runbook entries and playbook steps for manual override and forced fallback
Run staging chaos tests and capture dashboards and postmortem notes
decisions: Use active synthetic probes plus passive telemetry rather than passive-only detection to reduce warm-start risk
Certification token will have TTL of 5 minutes by default to balance safety and promotion latency
Promotion ramp will be policy-driven: default 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 minutes unless 'quick promote' flag enabled by SRE
Fallback model variants will be considered compatible only if quality regression on evaluation prompts < 3% by configured metric
Rollback strategy favors automated demote + traffic re-route to origin region; full cluster drain avoided unless manual approval
risks: False positives in synthetic probes could block valid promotions and increase customer-visible latency during incidents
Certification API may become a new single point of failure if not highly available and cached appropriately
Model-variant compatibility checks may miss edge-case prompts leading to silent quality regressions
Rapid promotion/rollback cycles could oscillate routing decisions if hysteresis is not tuned
